title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). Let Π = π̂_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. It carries the S_3 symmetries of the three punctures: an order-3 rotation ρ, with ρ(l_0) = l_1 where l_i are loops around the punctures, and an involution σ_∞ fixing ∞ and swapping 0 and 1. Grothendieck studies outer automorphisms u 'à lacets', i.e. those sending each inertia class to a power of itself, with a common multiplier μ = 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ*. Such a u, extended to the semidirect product with the symmetries, is encoded by three elements:
- g, defined by u(ρ) = gρ;
- h, defined by u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞;
- f ∈ L\Π, where L is the stabiliser at ∞ (the margin of the previous page says this is essentially the earlier h_0), defined by u(ε_0) = int(f^{-1})(ε_0^μ).
The 'formula (11)' (transcribed 'Carte', probably 'de base') ties them together: σ_∞(h) = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f).

This page treats the case h = 1, i.e. u commutes with σ_∞. Then (11) gives g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f).
- Put φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1>. It satisfies φ σ_∞(φ) = 1 automatically, since σ_∞ is an involution.
- Put ξ = l_0^ν φ. Using ρ(l_0) = l_1 one checks g = (l_0^ν f)^{-1} ξ ρ(l_0^ν f). This identity is correct: (l_0^ν f)^{-1} ξ = f^{-1}φ = σ_∞(f)^{-1}, and ρ(l_0^ν f) = l_1^ν ρ(f).
- Hence g is ρ-conjugate (twisted conjugate) to ξ. The requirement that u(ρ) again has order 3, namely g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1, is therefore equivalent to the cocycle equation ξ ρ(ξ) ρ^2(ξ) = 1 (13)/(15).
- Conclusion (16): outer automorphisms with inertia condition that commute with σ_∞ and have multiplier 2ν+1 correspond to pairs (φ, ξ) with φ σ_∞(φ) = 1 and ξ ρ(ξ) ρ^2(ξ) = 1, linked by the compatibility ξ = l_0^ν φ (14). For μ = 1 the compatibility is simply ξ = φ.
- f is recovered uniquely from φ via (12), and u is recovered from g via (17).
- The page then announces the symmetric analysis: automorphisms commuting with ρ (g = 1), described by (h, f). The next page carries this out, producing ψ = f ρ(f)^{-1} and η = l_0^{-ν} ψ.

In modern terms these are exactly the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1 and the 3-cycle (hexagon) relation f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1, with m = (λ−1)/2 = ν, which define Drinfeld's GT^ before the pentagon is imposed. Grothendieck writes them in a symmetric, cocycle form: a Z/2-cocycle and a Z/3-cocycle tied together by a power of an inertia generator.
errors: No genuine mathematical error found; the identity in (17) checks out under ρ(l_0) = l_1 and product notation l_0^ν·f.

Gap: 'f déterminé de façon unique en fonction de φ' needs two facts. Uniqueness only holds modulo the σ_∞-fixed subgroup L, consistent with f ∈ L\Π. Existence of f for every solution φ of φσ_∞(φ) = 1 needs triviality of the nonabelian H^1(Z/2, Π), i.e. conjugacy of all involutions in Π⋊⟨σ_∞⟩. This holds: the group is the profinite completion of Z/2 * Z, and finite subgroups of free profinite products are conjugate into factors. Grothendieck does not justify it on this page.
Similarly, passing from g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1 to the ξ equation uses ρ^3 = 1 on the nose (not just modulo inner automorphisms); this is implicit in the choice of lifts.

ideas.what: Encoding automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} (with inertia condition and multiplier 2ν+1) that commute with σ_∞ by pairs (φ, ξ) satisfying φσ_∞(φ) = 1, ξρ(ξ)ρ^2(ξ) = 1, ξ = l_0^ν φ
ideas.modern_name: 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations defining GT^ (without pentagon); S_3-equivariant description of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1991); S_3-symmetric reformulations by Lochak–Schneps, Harbater–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches the Teichmüller tower / Galois action; explicit relations of this form not in published texts to my knowledge. La Longue Marche (1981) discusses automorphisms of π_{0,3}; unsure whether these exact equations appear there.

ideas.what: Change of variables φ = fσ_∞(f)^{-1} and ξ = l_0^ν φ turning the equation for g into a twisted-conjugacy cocycle equation
ideas.modern_name: nonabelian group cohomology / twisted conjugacy for finite group actions on free profinite groups

ideas.what: Remark that for μ = 1 the compatibility collapses to ξ = φ
ideas.modern_name: trivial-multiplier (λ = 1) part of GT^, containing the image of the Galois commutator subgroup

missed.claim: Grothendieck, in notes plausibly from the early 1980s (pre-Drinfeld), derives the 2-cycle and hexagon relations of GT^ in a symmetric form: a Z/2-cocycle φ and a Z/3-cocycle ξ linked by ξ = l_0^ν φ, with multiplier μ = 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ*. This is essentially the 'GT_0' part of Drinfeld's definition, obtained independently via S_3-symmetries of π̂_{0,3}. Specialists (Lochak, Schneps) know Grothendieck anticipated parts of GT, but this explicit cocycle formulation and its compatibility condition are not, to my knowledge, attributed to him in print.
missed.quote: les automorphismes extérieurs de π̂_{0,3} qui commutent à σ_∞, avec multiplicateur μ_∞ = 2ν+1, correspondent aux couples de solutions (ξ,φ) des équations φσ_∞(φ)=1  ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 satisfaisant de plus la condition de compatibilité (14)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the defining relations of GT^. The symmetric 'pair of cocycles' presentation, with the dual description by (η, ψ) for automorphisms commuting with ρ on the next page, is a slightly different coordinate system from Drinfeld's. It could clarify the S_3-equivariant structure of GT and its relation to automorphisms of the orbifold groups of M_{0,4}/S_3.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct and amounts to a pre-Drinfeld derivation of the GT^ 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations in an S_3-symmetric cocycle form. That Grothendieck had GT-like ideas is known in the community, but these explicit equations from the unpublished sequel to La Longue Marche are a notable, probably uncredited detail. It is not a new theorem, though.
transcription_corrections: 'par la formule de Carte (11)' is probably 'par la formule de base (11)' (or similar); the referenced formula is the (11) relating g, f, ν.
In (17), 'l_0^ν f' and 'l_0^ν φ' denote products l_0^ν·f and l_0^ν·φ (consistent with the computation), not an action.
The left vertical margin note is roughly 'On trouve ... ξ ... φ ... [déterminent?] ...'; the transcription's placeholder is fine but its content is unreadable.

Line 'De façon symétrique, on va s'intéresser aux u de π̂_{0,3} qui commutent aux autom. à toutes ...' is better read as '... aux u de Π̂_{0,3} qui commutent aux autom...' continuing on the next page with 'tant à ρ' (i.e. 'commutant à ρ').
